# `nullable-pointer-length`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports allocating from a length paired with a nullable C pointer, then
returning the allocation uninitialized when the pointer is null.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

C APIs commonly require null to imply zero length. Failing to enforce that
contract exposes undefined bytes as initialized output.

## When it fires

Reject null with a positive length or initialize the output on every branch
before returning it.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn copy(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, ptr: ?[*]const u8, len: usize) ![]u8 {
    const out = try allocator.alloc(u8, len);
    if (ptr) |p| {
        @memcpy(out, p[0..len]);
    }
    return out;
}
```
